hadiths.arabicText:
وَحَدَّثَنِي ، عَنْ /12 مَالِك /12 ، عَنْ /94 يَحْيَى بْنِ سَعِيدٍ L8272 /94 ، /27 عَنِ /26 الْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ L1598 /26 ، " أَنَّ /20 رَجُلًا كَانَتْ تَحْتَهُ وَلِيدَةٌ لِقَوْمٍ ، فَقَالَ لِأَهْلِهَا : شَأْنَكُمْ بِهَا ، فَرَأَى النَّاسُ أَنَّهَا تَطْلِيقَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ " /27 * 
$1135  1138 /8

hadiths.english_translation: Malik said: He heard Ibn Shihab saying regarding a man who says to his wife 'You are absolved from me and I am absolved from you': 'It is three divorces, of the same status as al-Battah (irrevocable).' Malik said regarding a man who says to his wife 'You are Khaliyyah (free), or Bariyyah (absolved), or Ba'inah (separated)': It is three divorces for the woman he has consummated the marriage with, and he should be questioned under oath regarding the woman he has not consummated the marriage with - did he intend one or three? If he says one, he is made to swear an oath on that, and he becomes one of the suitors, because nothing makes the woman whom her husband has consummated the marriage with free, separated, or absolved except three divorces, while the woman he has not consummated the marriage with, one divorce makes her free, absolved, and separated. Malik said: This is the best of what I have heard regarding that.

potential_issues.issue: Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri is classified as a mudallis (category 3 in Ibn Hajar's classification), though the term used here is 'yaqulu' (saying) which is ambiguous.
potential_issues.impact: Minimal impact as al-Zuhri is extremely reliable despite occasional tadlis, and Malik explicitly states he heard from him (sama'). Al-Zuhri is considered among the most trustworthy scholars of his generation. The report is also al-Zuhri's own legal opinion, not a narration from earlier sources.

potential_issues.issue: This is primarily Malik's own legal reasoning and opinion (ijtihad) based on what he heard from Ibn Shihab, making it a statement of fiqh rather than pure hadith transmission.
potential_issues.impact: This affects classification as scholarly opinion rather than prophetic tradition, but does not affect the authenticity of the transmission itself.

hadiths.arabicText:
وَحَدَّثَنِي ، عَنْ /12 مَالِك /12 ، /27 أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ /26 ابْنَ شِهَابٍ /26 ، يَقُولُ فِي الرَّجُلِ يَقُولُ لِامْرَأَتِهِ بَرِئْتِ مِنِّي وَبَرِئْتُ مِنْكِ : /20 " إِنَّهَا ثَلَاثُ تَطْلِيقَاتٍ ، بِمَنْزِلَةِ الْبَتَّةِ " /27 . قَالَ /12 مَالِكٌ /12 ، فِي الرَّجُلِ يَقُولُ لِامْرَأَتِهِ أَنْتِ خَلِيَّةٌ أَوْ بَرِيَّةٌ أَوْ بَائِنَةٌ : /10 إِنَّهَا ثَلَاثُ تَطْلِيقَاتٍ لِلْمَرْأَةِ الَّتِي قَدْ دَخَلَ بِهَا ، وَيُدَيَّنُ فِي الَّتِي لَمْ يَدْخُلْ بِهَا ، أَوَاحِدَةً أَرَادَ ، أَمْ ثَلَاثًا ؟ فَإِنْ قَالَ وَاحِدَةً ، أُحْلِفَ عَلَى ذَلِكَ ، وَكَانَ خَاطِبًا مِنَ الْخُطَّابِ ، لِأَنَّهُ لَا يُخْلِي الْمَرْأَةَ الَّتِي قَدْ دَخَلَ بِهَا زَوْجُهَا ، وَلَا يُبِينُهَا وَلَا يُبْرِيهَا ، إِلَّا ثَلَاثُ تَطْلِيقَاتٍ ، وَالَّتِي لَمْ يَدْخُلْ بِهَا تُخْلِيهَا وَتُبْرِيهَا ، وَتُبِينُهَا الْوَاحِدَةُ /10 . قَالَ /12 مَالِكٌ /12 : /10 وَهَذَا أَحْسَنُ مَا سَمِعْتُ فِي ذَلِكَ /10 * 
 E287

hadiths.english_translation: It reached Malik: That a man came to Abdullah ibn Umar and said: 'O Abu Abd al-Rahman, I placed the matter of my wife in her hand, and she divorced herself, so what do you see?' Abdullah ibn Umar said: 'I see it as she said.' The man said: 'Do not do so, O Abu Abd al-Rahman.' Ibn Umar said: 'I do it? You did it!'

chainIssues: The chain is mursal/disconnected with the term 'balaghahu' (it reached him), meaning Malik did not specify his source between himself and the incident involving Ibn Umar.

potential_issues.issue: The chain uses 'balaghahu' (it reached him), which indicates a mursal/munqati' (disconnected) transmission. Malik does not specify who informed him of this incident.

The balaghat of Imam Malik are generally considered somewhat reliable due to his strict standards, but they are weaker than his connected chains. Scholars differ on accepting Malik's balaghat - some accept them due to his reliability, while others require supporting evidence.

potential_issues.issue: We do not know who the intermediary narrators are between Malik and the incident with Ibn Umar, making it impossible to evaluate their reliability.
potential_issues.impact: This prevents full authentication of the chain using classical hadith methodology. The report depends on trust in Malik's standards for what he accepts and transmits.

hadiths.arabicText:
حَدَّثَنِي /22 يَحْيَى /22 ، عَنْ /12 مَالِكٍ /12 ، أَنَّهُ بَلَغَهُ ، /27 أَنَّ رَجُلًا جَاءَ إِلَى عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُمَرَ ، فَقَالَ : يَا أَبَا عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ ، إِنِّي جَعَلْتُ أَمْرَ امْرَأَتِي فِي يَدِهَا ، فَطَلَّقَتْ نَفْسَهَا ، فَمَاذَا تَرَى ؟ فَقَالَ /93 عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عُمَرَ /93 : /20 " أُرَاهُ كَمَا قَالَتْ " ، فَقَالَ الرَّجُلُ : لَا تَفْعَلْ يَا أَبَا عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ ، فَقَالَ ابْنُ عُمَرَ : أَنَا أَفْعَلُ أَنْتَ فَعَلْتَهُ /27 * 
$1137  1140 /3

hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Abdullah ibn Umar: He used to say: 'When a man gives his wife authority over her matter, then the judgment is what she judges with it, unless he denies it and says: I only intended one (divorce), then he swears an oath on that, and he has more right to her as long as she is in her waiting period (iddah).'

hadiths.arabicText: وَحَدَّثَنِي ، عَنْ /12 مَالِك /12 ، عَنْ /94 نَافِعٍ L7863 /94 ، /27 أَنَّ /93 عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ عُمَرَ L4967 /93 ، كَانَ يَقُولُ : /20 " إِذَا مَلَّكَ الرَّجُلُ امْرَأَتَهُ أَمْرَهَا ، فَالْقَضَاءُ مَا قَضَتْ بِهِ ، إِلَّا أَنْ يُنْكِرَ عَلَيْهَا ، وَيَقُولُ : لَمْ أُرِدْ إِلَّا وَاحِدَةً ، فَيَحْلِفُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ ، وَيَكُونُ أَمْلَكَ بِهَا مَا كَانَتْ فِي عِدَّتِهَا " /27 *

hadiths.english_translation: Sa'id ibn Sulayman ibn Zayd ibn Thabit narrated from Kharijah ibn Zayd ibn Thabit that he informed him: He was sitting with Zayd ibn Thabit when Muhammad ibn Abi Atiq came to him with tears flowing from his eyes. Zayd said to him: 'What is your matter?' He said: 'I gave my wife authority over her matter, and she separated from me.' Zayd said to him: 'What made you do that?' He said: 'Al-Qadar (divine decree).' Zayd said: 'Take her back if you wish, for it is only one (divorce), and you have more right to her.'

حَدَّثَنِي /22 يَحْيَى /22 ، عَنْ /12 مَالِك /12 ، عَنْ /94 سَعِيدِ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ زَيْدِ بْنِ ثَابِتٍ L3340 /94 ، عَنْ /26 خَارِجَةَ بْنِ زَيْدِ بْنِ ثَابِتٍ L2607 /26 أَنَّهُ أَخْبَرَهُ : /27 أَنَّهُ كَانَ جَالِسًا عِنْدَ زَيْدِ بْنِ ثَابِتٍ ، فَأَتَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَبِي عَتِيقٍ وَعَيْنَاهُ تَدْمَعَانِ ، فَقَالَ لَهُ زَيْدٌ : " مَا شَأْنُكَ ؟ " فَقَالَ : مَلَّكْتُ امْرَأَتِي أَمْرَهَا ، فَفَارَقَتْنِي ، فَقَالَ لَهُ زَيْدٌ : " مَا حَمَلَكَ عَلَى ذَلِكَ ؟ " قَالَ : الْقَدَرُ ، فَقَالَ /93 زَيْدٌ L3131 /93 : /20 " ارْتَجِعْهَا إِنْ شِئْتَ ، فَإِنَّمَا هِيَ وَاحِدَةٌ وَأَنْتَ أَمْلَكُ بِهَا " /27 * 
$1139  1142 /8

hadiths.english_translation: Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim narrated from his father: That a man from Thaqif gave his wife authority over her matter. She said: 'You are the divorce.' He remained silent. Then she said: 'You are the divorce.' He said: 'May a stone be in your mouth.' Then she said: 'You are the divorce.' He said: 'May a stone be in your mouth.' They disputed before Marwan ibn al-Hakam, and he made him swear that he only gave her authority over one (divorce), and returned her to him. Malik said: Abd al-Rahman said: 'Al-Qasim used to admire this judgment and considered it the best of what he heard regarding that.' Malik said: 'This is the best of what I have heard regarding that, and the most beloved to me.'

وَحَدَّثَنِي ، عَنْ /12 مَالِك /12 ، عَنْ /94 عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ الْقَاسِمِ /94 ، عَنْ /26 أَبِيهِ /26 ، /27 أَنَّ رَجُلًا مِنْ ثَقِيفٍ مَلَّكَ امْرَأَتَهُ أَمْرَهَا ، فَقَالَتْ : أَنْتَ الطَّلَاقُ ، فَسَكَتَ ، ثُمّ قَالَتْ : أَنْتَ الطَّلَاقُ ، فَقَالَ : بِفِيكِ الْحَجَرُ ، ثُمّ قَالَتْ : أَنْتَ الطَّلَاقُ ، فَقَالَ : بِفَيكِ الْحَجَرُ ، فَاخْتَصَمَا إِلَى /26 مَرْوَانَ بْنِ الْحَكَمِ /26 ، /20 " فَاسْتَحْلَفَهُ مَا مَلَّكَهَا إِلَّا وَاحِدَةً ، وَرَدَّهَا إِلَيْهِ " /27 . قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 : /10 قَالَ عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ : فَكَانَ الْقَاسِمُ يُعْجِبُهُ هَذَا الْقَضَاءُ ، وَيَرَاهُ أَحْسَنَ مَا سَمِعَ فِي ذَلِكَ /10 . قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 : /10 وَهَذَا أَحْسَنُ مَا سَمِعْتُ فِي ذَلِكَ ، وَأَحَبُّهُ إِلَيَّ /10 * 
E288

hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Aisha, the Mother of the Believers: She arranged the marriage of Quraybah bint Abi Umayyah to Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr, and they married him. Then they blamed Abd al-Rahman and said: 'We only married (her) because of Aisha.' Aisha sent to Abd al-Rahman and mentioned that to him. He placed the matter of Quraybah in her (Quraybah's) hand, and she chose her husband, so that was not a divorce.

Wife choosing to remain with husband when given authority
hadiths.arabicText:
حَدَّثَنِي /22 يَحْيَى /22 ، عَنْ /12 مَالِك /12 ، عَنْ /94 عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ الْقَاسِمِ L4312 /94 ، عَنْ /26 أَبِيهِ L1598 /26 ، /27 عَنْ /93 عَائِشَةَ L4049 /93 أُمِّ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ : أَنَّهَا خَطَبَتْ عَلَى عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي بَكْرٍ ، /64 قُرَيْبَةَ بِنْتَ أَبِي أُمَيَّةَ /64 ، فَزَوَّجُوهُ ، ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمْ عَتَبُوا عَلَى عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ ، وَقَالُوا : مَا زَوَّجْنَا إِلَّا /64 عَائِشَةَ /64 ، فَأَرْسَلَتْ /64 عَائِشَةُ /64 إِلَى عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ ، فَذَكَرَتْ ذَلِكَ لَهُ ، /20 " فَجَعَلَ أَمْرَ /64 قُرَيْبَةَ /64 بِيَدِهَا ، فَاخْتَارَتْ زَوْجَهَا ، فَلَمْ يَكُنْ ذَلِكَ طَلَاقًا " /27 * 
$1141  1144 /3

hadiths.english_translation: Narrated that Aisha, wife of the Prophet ﷺ, married Hafsah bint Abd al-Rahman to al-Mundhir ibn al-Zubayr while Abd al-Rahman was absent in al-Sham (Syria). When Abd al-Rahman came, he said: 'Would someone like me have this done to him? Would someone like me be acted upon without consultation?' Aisha spoke to al-Mundhir ibn al-Zubayr, and al-Mundhir said: 'That is in the hand of Abd al-Rahman.' Abd al-Rahman said: 'I would not refuse a matter that you have decided.' So Hafsah remained with al-Mundhir, and that was not a divorce.

plainChains: Yahya -> Malik -> Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim -> his father al-Qasim -> (report about Aisha)

potential_issues.issue: The chain uses 'anna (أَنَّ) when reporting about Aisha, which can indicate indirect transmission or a report about someone rather than from them directly.
potential_issues.impact: Minor impact. Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad was Aisha's nephew and lived in her household, making him a direct witness to her actions and statements. However, the use of 'anna suggests this might be a report about what Aisha did rather than her direct narration. The chain remains strong for transmitting the incident.

potential_issues.issue: Uses 'an (عَنْ) throughout the chain before the final 'anna.
potential_issues.impact: Minimal impact as all narrators are highly reliable and the family connections (grandson to grandmother, son to father) make direct transmission certain.

Topics: Incident of Aisha arranging marriage during guardian's absence
Marriage of Hafsah bint Abd al-Rahman to al-Mundhir ibn al-Zubayr
Guardian's response to marriage arranged in his absence
hadiths.arabicText:
وَحَدَّثَنِي ، عَنْ /12 مَالِك /12 ، عَنْ /94 عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ الْقَاسِمِ L4312 /94 ، عَنْ /26 أَبِيهِ L1598 /26 ، /27 أَنَّ /93 عَائِشَةَ L4049 /93 زَوْجَ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ زَوَّجَتْ /64 حَفْصَةَ بِنْتَ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ /64 ، الْمُنْذِرَ بْنَ الزُّبَيْرِ ، وَعَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ غَائِبٌ /60 بِالشَّامِ /60 ، فَلَمَّا قَدِمَ عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ ، قَالَ : وَمِثْلِي يُصْنَعُ هَذَا بِهِ ، وَمِثْلِي يُفْتَاتُ عَلَيْهِ ، فَكَلَّمَتْ /64 عَائِشَةُ /64 ، الْمُنْذِرَ بْنَ الزُّبَيْرِ ، فَقَالَ الْمُنْذِرُ : فَإِنَّ ذَلِكَ بِيَدِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ ، فَقَالَ عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ : /20 " مَا كُنْتُ لِأَرُدَّ أَمْرًا قَضَيْتِيهِ " ، فَقَرَّتْ /64 حَفْصَةُ /64 عِنْدَ الْمُنْذِرِ ، وَلَمْ يَكُنْ ذَلِكَ طَلَاقًا /27 * 
$1142  1145 /3

hadiths.english_translation: It reached Malik: That Abdullah ibn Umar and Abu Hurayrah were asked about the man who gives his wife authority over her matter, and she returns it to him without deciding anything regarding it. They said: 'That is not a divorce.'

chainIssues: The chain is mursal/disconnected with the term 'balaghahu' (it reached him), meaning Malik did not specify his source between himself and the statement of Ibn Umar and Abu Hurayrah.

plainChains: Yahya -> Malik -> [unknown intermediary/intermediaries] -> Abdullah ibn Umar and Abu Hurayrah

potential_issues.issue: The chain uses 'balaghahu' (it reached him), which indicates a mursal/munqati' (disconnected) transmission. Malik does not specify who informed him of this statement from Ibn Umar and Abu Hurayrah.
potential_issues.impact: Significant impact on chain integrity. This creates a clear gap in the transmission. While Malik's balaghat are generally treated with some consideration due to his strict standards, they remain weaker than connected chains. The absence of the intermediary prevents full authentication.

potential_issues.issue: Unknown intermediary narrators between Malik and the two companions, making reliability assessment of those links impossible.
potential_issues.impact: This prevents complete chain authentication using classical hadith methodology.

Topics: Statement of Ibn Umar and Abu Hurayrah on delegated divorce
Wife returning divorce authority without using it
hadiths.arabicText:
وَحَدَّثَنِي ، عَنْ /12 مَالِكٍ /12 ، أَنَّهُ بَلَغَهُ ، /27 أَنَّ /93 عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ عُمَرَ /93 ، /93 وَأَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ /93 ، سُئِلَا عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يُمَلِّكُ امْرَأَتَهُ أَمْرَهَا ، فَتَرُدُّ بِذَلِكَ إِلَيْهِ ، وَلَا تَقْضِي فِيهِ شَيْئًا ؟ فَقَالَا : /20 " لَيْسَ ذَلِكَ بِطَلَاقٍ " /27 * 
$1143  1146 /8

hadiths.english_translation: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: 'When a man gives his wife authority over her matter and she does not separate from him and remains with him, that is not a divorce.' Malik said regarding the woman given authority when her husband gives her authority over her matter, then they separate and she does not accept anything from that: 'There is nothing in her hand from that, and it is for her as long as they remain in their sitting.'

The report is also Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab's own legal opinion.

hadiths.arabicText:
وَحَدَّثَنِي ، عَنْ /12 مَالِك /12 ، عَنْ /94 يَحْيَى بْنِ سَعِيدٍ L8272 /94 ، /27 عَنْ /26 سَعِيدِ بْنِ الْمُسَيَّبِ L3299 /26 ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ : /20 " إِذَا مَلَّكَ الرَّجُلُ امْرَأَتَهُ ، أَمْرَهَا فَلَمْ تُفَارِقْهُ ، وَقَرَّتْ عِنْدَهُ ، فَلَيْسَ ذَلِكَ بِطَلَاقٍ " /27 . قَالَ /12 مَالِكٌ /12 فِي الْمُمَلَّكَةِ إِذَا مَلَّكَهَا زَوْجُهَا أَمْرَهَا ، ثُمَّ افْتَرَقَا ، وَلَمْ تَقْبَلْ مِنْ ذَلِكَ شَيْئًا : /10 فَلَيْسَ بِيَدِهَا مِنْ ذَلِكَ شَيْءٌ ، وَهُوَ لَهَا مَا دَامَا فِي مَجْلِسِهِمَا /10 * 
:E289

hadiths.english_translation: Narrated that Ali ibn Abi Talib used to say: 'When a man takes an oath (ila') from his wife, no divorce falls upon him even if the four months pass, until he is stopped (by the judge). Then either he divorces or he returns (to his wife).' Malik said: 'That is the practice with us.'

narrators.full_name: Ali ibn Abi Talib ibn Abd al-Muttalib ibn Hashim al-Qurashi al-Hashimi

plainChains: Yahya -> Malik -> Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq -> his father Muhammad al-Baqir -> Ali ibn Abi Talib

potential_issues.issue: Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq is graded as Saduq (truthful) rather than Thiqah by the majority of hadith scholars. While he was a great scholar and jurist, some hadith critics noted occasional issues with precision in transmission.
potential_issues.impact: Moderate impact. Ja'far al-Sadiq was highly knowledgeable but not considered among the most precise hadith transmitters. His narrations are generally acceptable but not at the highest level of authentication. Imam Malik knew him personally and selected what he transmitted from him carefully.

potential_issues.issue: The entire chain uses 'an (عَنْ) throughout, which are ambiguous transmission terms.
potential_issues.impact: Minor to moderate impact. While 'an is ambiguous, the family chain (great-great-grandson -> great-grandson -> grandson -> grandfather -> Ali) provides natural connection. However, there are scholarly debates about whether Muhammad al-Baqir actually heard from his grandfather Ali directly, as Ali died when Muhammad al-Baqir was very young (around 3-4 years old). This creates a potential disconnect in the chain.

potential_issues.issue: Potential issue of sama' (direct hearing): Muhammad al-Baqir from Ali ibn Abi Talib. Ali died in 40 AH and Muhammad al-Baqir was born around 57 AH according to some accounts, or 56 AH according to others. If these dates are correct, direct hearing would be impossible.
potential_issues.impact: Significant impact if the dates make direct hearing impossible. However, some scholars place Muhammad al-Baqir's birth earlier (around 56-57 AH is debated), and there are differing accounts. The majority view is that he did not meet Ali directly, making this chain munqati' (disconnected). This would be a major issue affecting the chain's integrity.

Topics: Statement of Ali ibn Abi Talib on Ila' (oath of sexual abstinence)
Legal ruling on the four-month waiting period in Ila'
Judicial process for resolving Ila' situations
hadiths.arabicText:
حَدَّثَنِي /22 يَحْيَى /22 ، عَنْ /12 مَالِك /12 ، عَنْ /94 جَعْفَرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ L2163 /94 ، عَنْ /26 أَبِيهِ L7187 /26 ، /27 عَنْ /93 عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي طَالِبٍ L5722 /93 ، أَنَّهُ كَانَ يَقُولُ : /20 " إِذَا آلَى الرَّجُلُ مِنَ امْرَأَتِهِ ، لَمْ يَقَعْ عَلَيْهِ طَلَاقٌ ، وَإِنْ مَضَتِ الْأَرْبَعَةُ الْأَشْهُرِ حَتَّى يُوقَفَ ، فَإِمَّا أَنْ يُطَلِّقَ ، وَإِمَّا أَنْ يَفِيءَ " /27 . قَالَ /12 مَالِكٌ /12 : /10 وَذَلِكَ الْأَمْرُ عِنْدَنَا /10 * 
$1145  1148 /3
